title: Support Measures for Phase Two (Heightened Alert) and Phase Three (Heightened Alert)
what_it_is: Support Measures for Phase Two (Heightened Alert) and Phase Three (Heightened Alert)

sections.label: Rolling waves of infections
sections.summary: Rolling waves of infections continue worldwide, driven by new variants; Delta is estimated 60% more transmissible than Alpha, about two and a half times more contagious than the original strain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Each time you think you have it under control, it comes storming back.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we are continuing to see rolling waves of infections around the world, driven by new variants of the virus Late last year, we had the Alpha variant, which was first detected in the United Kingdom, and which was about 50% more transmissible than the original strain detected in Wuhan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Now, we are dealing with the Delta variant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is estimated to be 60% more transmissible than the Alpha variant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That means it is about two and a half times more contagious than the original strain.

sections.label: mRNA vaccines against Delta
sections.summary: The mRNA vaccines, Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna, offer excellent protection against severe illness, even with the Delta variant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The good news is that the mRNA vaccines, be it Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna, offer excellent protection against severe illness, even with the Delta variant.

sections.label: Phase Two Heightened Alert
sections.summary: With new clusters at Tan Tock Seng Hospital and Changi Airport and a sustained increase in unlinked community cases, Singapore moved into Phase Two (Heightened Alert) on 16 May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Instead, we adopted more targeted measures calibrated based on the severity of the outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, in early to mid-May, we saw the emergence of new clusters, most notably at Tan Tock Seng Hospital and Changi Airport, and a sustained increase in unlinked community cases, we moved into Phase Two (Heightened Alert) on 16 May to protect Singaporeans and to control the spread of the virus.

sections.label: Easing restrictions from June
sections.summary: The additional measures curbed the virus spread while most of the economy continued operating, so restrictions eased from 14 June to Phase Three (Heightened Alert), with further opening expected from 12 July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These additional measures have worked in curbing the spread of the virus, while allowing most parts of the economy to continue operating.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we started to ease the restrictions from 14 June, when we moved from Phase Two to Phase Three (Heightened Alert); and we expect to open up further from 12 July to allow larger groups of five people to dine together.

sections.label: Support for hawkers and workers
sections.summary: Subsidies for table cleaning and centralised dishwashing services were provided to hawkers, and a COVID-19 Recovery Grant (Temporary) scheme gave short-term support to employees and self-employed persons with sudden income loss.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To further assist our hawkers who were impacted by the dine-in restrictions, we provided subsidies for table cleaning and centralised dishwashing services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We also introduced a COVID-19 Recovery Grant (Temporary), or CRG-T, scheme to provide short-term support to employees and self-employed persons who suffered from sudden and significant income loss during this period.

sections.label: Cost of support measures
sections.summary: The additional support measures for the period of Heightened Alert are expected to cost $1.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The additional support measures for the period of Heightened Alert are expected to cost $1.2 billion.

sections.label: Past reserves for crisis response
sections.summary: Setting aside resources for rainy days has strengthened the fiscal position, with up to $53.7 billion expected to be drawn from past reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But it is precisely this discipline of setting aside resources for rainy days that has put us in a strong fiscal position to respond decisively to the current crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We already expect to draw up to $53.7 billion from our past reserves.

sections.label: Reallocation from SINGA capitalisation
sections.summary: The Bill seeks reallocation, not new monies, with about $0.6 billion of the $1.2 billion from capitalisation of development expenditure under SINGA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is the responsible way to manage our finances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we are not asking for new monies in this Bill but are seeking a reallocation of monies to fund the support package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: About $0.6 billion out of the $1.2 billion will come from the capitalisation of development expenditure under the Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act, or SINGA, in short.

sections.label: Reallocation from delayed development projects
sections.summary: The remaining $0.6 billion will be reallocated from underutilisation of development expenditure mainly due to COVID-19 project delays.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The remaining $0.6 billion will be reallocated from underutilisation of development expenditure mainly due to delays in projects arising from COVID-19.

sections.label: Supplementary Supply Bill reallocation
sections.summary: The Supplementary Supply Bill is introduced to effect a total reallocation of $1.2 billion to fund the support package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But, in the meantime, there is some fiscal space for reallocation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why I am introducing this Supplementary Supply Bill to effect the total reallocation of $1.2 billion to fund the support package.

sections.label: JSS payments to SMEs
sections.summary: About two-thirds of the $26.7 billion of JSS paid out to-date went to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, about two-thirds of the $26.7 billion of JSS paid out to-date went to SMEs.

sections.label: Extension of loan schemes
sections.summary: The Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and Enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme – Trade Loan are extended six months, from 1 October 2021 to 31 March 2022, with unchanged parameters including 70% Government risk-share.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: While economic conditions have improved, such access to credit remains critical to our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I will extend the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and the Enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme – Trade Loan for an additional six months from 1 October 2021 to 31 March 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The parameters for both schemes remain unchanged, including the Government risk-share of 70%.

sections.label: Funding of measures
sections.summary: The Government will fund the measures by reallocating Ministries' budgets, costing about $1.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Government will fund these measures by reallocating the budget of various Ministries and the measures will cost about $1.2 billion.

sections.label: SME loan schemes extended
sections.summary: The Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and Enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme Trade Loan are extended six months to 31 March next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To continue to help SMEs in need, I will extend the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and the Enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme Trade Loan for an additional six months to 31 March next year.

sections.label: GDP growth forecast
sections.summary: Barring unforeseen circumstances, GDP growth of at least 4% to 6% is expected this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, barring unforeseen circumstances, we continue to expect GDP growth of at least 4% to 6% this year.

sections.label: Targeted industry support and deficit
sections.summary: Targeted support continues for industries to preserve capabilities and position them for recovery, with an expected deficit of $11 billion or 2.2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the same time, we will continue to provide targeted support for these industries to preserve their core capabilities and to position them for recovery, which will come when travel restrictions are eventually lifted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We expect an overall deficit of $11 billion or 2.2% of GDP – similar to what was previously announced at Budget 2021.

sections.label: Vaccination and reopening plans
sections.summary: Priority is speeding up vaccinations to reach high coverage, enabling progressive reopening and travel corridor discussions for vaccinated persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we are also very mindful that if we were to reopen prematurely before we reach high enough vaccination levels, we could end up with another wave of infections and, worse, a surge in hospitalisation and ICU cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, our priority is to speed up vaccinations and we have the ability to reach a very high level of vaccination coverage over the next one or two months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This will enable us to progressively reopen and reconnect with the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are already discussing with other jurisdictions that have effectively controlled the infection to work out travel corridors with them for vaccinated persons to travel more freely, either without the need for Stay-Home Notice (SHN) or with a reduced SHN duration.

sections.label: Private-public collaborations scaled up
sections.summary: The Emerging Stronger Taskforce prototyped Alliances for Action, and more such private-public collaborations will be scaled up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In this regard, I am glad that the Emerging Stronger Task force has prototyped the Alliances for Action, where groups of private and public stakeholders come together to identify opportunities and create new solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will build on this prototype and scale up more of such private-public collaborations.

sections.label: COVID-19 living normally roadmap
sections.summary: COVID-19 is unlikely to go away soon, but vaccinations and better treatment can make SARS-CoV-2 resemble influenza, and Singapore is preparing a roadmap to live normally with it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The reality is that COVID-19 is unlikely to go away anytime soon.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But with vaccinations and with improvements in treatment, we can make SARS-CoV-2 look more like influenza in terms of morbidity and mortality.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As my fellow Multi-Ministry Task force (MTF) Co-Chairs and I have shared, we are preparing a roadmap for Singapore to transit to such a scenario where we learn to live normally with COVID-19.

sections.label: Singapore vaccination targets for seniors
sections.summary: Recent cases rose mostly from the Delta variant without higher hospitalisation rates due to vaccine protection, and Singapore targets two-thirds of its population fully vaccinated by National Day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It has seen a recent rise in cases, mostly due to the Delta variant, but the new outbreaks have not led to higher hospitalisation rates because of the protection from the vaccine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, for Singapore, we are targeting for two-thirds of our population to be fully vaccinated by National Day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are also going all out to engage our seniors and get more of them vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have already reached higher than two-thirds for our seniors but it is not high enough and we want to get an even higher rate.
